summary: Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2013) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and has served as a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.
Rory Brendan Lindsay works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and held a teaching post at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, also studying under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (~1978–1983) and held posts at Clare College, Cambridge (~1987–2006) and the University of Oxford (~2006), becoming a British Academy Fellow in 2020.

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from 1960 to ~1969. He served at Komazawa University as assistant (1969), lecturer (1972), assistant professor (1977), and professor (1983–2012), and directed the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the Free University of Brussels (~1955–1959) and under Ludo Rocher (~1959–1965), later working at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970) and the University of Pennsylvania (from 1970).

Rosemarie Fuchs works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (attested 2000), and was a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist. She earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg and completed her Habilitation at Regensburg; she held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994), Jena (1994–2013), and Berlin (2013), and led the Society for Indo-European Studies (2004–2016).
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1958–1965). She held a post at Howard University from ~1965 to 1976.

Rosina Pastore specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, where she also worked as an assistant and PhD candidate.

Ross Bolleter works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Western Australia (~1964–1967) and trained under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken (1982–1992), later serving as a Zen teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1991–2023).

Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology who earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as chair of anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1997–2003) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2003–2010) under Gary A. Tubb, later holding a post at Tel Aviv University (~2010).

Roy W. Perrett is a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at the University of Canterbury (~1970–1975) and the University of Otago (~1980–1984), holding posts at Massey University (~1987–2000), the University of Hawaiʻi (~2001–2008), and the University of Melbourne (~2008).

Royall Tyler works in Japanology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Columbia, where Donald Keene supervised his doctorate, he taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Oslo, and headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, he taught at Sophia, Southern Methodist University, and Ryukoku University.
Rudolf Geiger studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from ~1913 to 1918. He later held an academic post at the University of Munich from ~1937 to 1958.

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the Köllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1839), and the University of Berlin (~1841–1843), later holding a post at Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.
